newsitem.title: USA: Ivory cocoa arrivals seen at 435,000 T to Dec 14.
newsitem.headline: Ivory cocoa arrivals seen at 435,000 T to Dec 14.

text.p: Total Ivory Coast cocoa arrivals reached some 435,000 tonnes through December 14, compared with 545,000 tonnes at the same time last year, trade house General Cocoa said in a weekly report.
The estimate, published in General Cocoa's newsletter dated December 20, and based on reports from "reliable market sources", is about 50,000 tonnes greater than previously thought.
"Ivory Coast arrivals were 50,000 tonnes more than the privately 'guesstimated' figures circulating in the market," the newsletter said.
Total 1996/97 Ivorian production was seen surpassing 1.0 million tonnes, against a record 1.22 million tonnes in 1995/96.
Scattered rains in the cocoa growing regions in Ivory Coast have led to an improved outlook for the 1997 mid-crop, the report said.
Ivory Coast is the world's leading grower of cocoa, producing around 40 percent of annual global outturn.
